$comment: Demo data (CLAUDE.md 1.2). Recorded attempts the fake judge replays when the prototype submits code. The first rule whose pattern matches the code wins; pseudo code replays the pseudo attempt.

findings.title: The last missing entry is dropped
findings.body: Line 18 slices off the final element, so a statement that misses only the last ledger entry reports nothing.

findings.title: Matching is quadratic
findings.body: Every ledger entry scans the whole statement. Index the statement by reference once, then each lookup is constant time.

findings.title: One statement line confirms many entries
findings.body: A matched line is never consumed, so two identical ledger entries are both confirmed by one line.

findings.title: A loop does nothing
findings.body: Lines 8 and 9 iterate the statement without using it.

findings.title: A list stands in for a set
findings.body: `seen` is only iterated; a list of tuples is fine, but the name suggests a membership test.

findings.title: The key is built twice in spirit
findings.body: Line 5 and line 8 both build a (reference, cents) pair; a small helper keeps the two definitions from drifting.

counter.praise: Linear, and duplicates are consumed one line at a time.

probe.skipped: Skipped because 2 hidden tests failed. Timing a wrong answer measures nothing useful.

findings.title: Touching bookings stay apart
findings.body: Line 9 compares with `<`, so a booking that starts the minute the last one ends opens a new block. The statement says touching bookings merge.

findings.title: Name the comparison
findings.body: The lambda on line 4 sorts by start; a named key reads faster.

findings.title: Name the comparison
findings.body: The lambda on line 4 sorts by start; a named key reads faster.

clean.praise: Linear after the sort, and every edge case handled.

findings.title: Empty input returns a reading that does not exist
findings.body: Line 10 falls back to `readings[0]` when no window fits. With no readings that is `undefined`; with fewer than k readings it invents a window. Return the empty list.

findings.title: shift() makes the deque linear per step
findings.body: Array.shift on line 7 moves every element. On a million readings with a wide window the total cost is quadratic, which case 13 shows as a time limit.

findings.title: dq is short for nothing
findings.body: Call it `candidates` and the loop explains itself.

clean.praise: Linear, and the empty case falls out of the loop on its own.

findings.title: Conflicts are treated as retries
findings.body: Lines 6 and 7 skip any repeated key without comparing account and amount, so a request that reuses a key for a different payment is silently dropped instead of rejected.

findings.title: rejected is never written
findings.body: The list on line 4 is returned but nothing appends to it, which hides the missing branch above.

float.problemTitle: Split a bill to the cent

findings.title: Shares do not add up to the total
findings.body: Rounding each share on its own loses or invents cents. Three equal shares of 1000 come to 999. Round down, then hand out the remainder by largest fraction.

findings.title: Large totals lose precision
findings.body: `total * w` exceeds 2^53 for totals near 10^12 with large weights, so the result is no longer exact. Use BigInt for the product.

exact.problemTitle: Split a bill to the cent

findings.title: The negative sort key needs a word
findings.body: Line 7 negates the remainder so the sort puts the largest first. A one-line comment or `key=` with `reverse` says the same thing in plain terms.

findings.title: Refill truncates to whole seconds
findings.body: `since / 1000` on line 11 is integer division, so 600 ms refills nothing. The bucket refills continuously; divide as a double.

findings.title: The bucket can overfill
findings.body: Nothing caps `t` at capacity after a refill, so a quiet client banks unlimited tokens.

median.problemTitle: Slowest endpoints in an access log

findings.title: Median of an even count takes the upper middle
findings.body: Line 9 picks index len // 2, which for two values is the larger one. The median of 30 and 50 is 40.

findings.title: Ties are not broken by name
findings.body: Line 10 sorts by median only, so equal medians keep dictionary order instead of name order.

probe.skipped: Skipped because 1 hidden test hit the time limit.

findings.title: Membership test on a list inside the search
findings.body: `goal in lines[line]` on line 14 scans the whole line every time it is dequeued. Build a set per line once; case 11 has lines with tens of thousands of stops.

findings.title: Stations are expanded more than once
findings.body: Lines 16 and 17 revisit stations already expanded through another line. Mark stations as seen too.

findings.title: Greedy is not optimal for these coins
findings.body: Taking the largest coin first works for some coin systems, not all. With 1, 5 and 12, fifteen takes four coins greedily and three optimally. This needs dynamic programming over amounts.

dp.praise: Exact on every coin system, and the sentinel is chosen with care.

zero.problemTitle: Two transfers that net to zero

findings.title: The current transfer is recorded before it is matched
findings.body: Line 6 stores index j before line 7 looks up its negation, so for two zeros the lookup finds j itself and the guard rejects it. Look up first, then record.

pseudo.problemTitle: Two transfers that net to zero
pseudo.code:
function netZeroPair(cents)
  seen <- empty map from amount to index
  for j from 0 to length(cents) - 1
    if seen has -cents[j]
      return [seen[-cents[j]], j]
    if seen does not have cents[j]
      seen[cents[j]] <- j
  return []
end

findings.title: The loop bound is spelled out by hand
findings.body: Line 3 counts to length minus one; "for each amount at index j" says the same with less to check.

findings.title: Sorting every merchant to keep k
findings.body: Line 7 sorts all merchants. With a million merchants and k of ten, a bounded heap does less work; the measured growth is still inside the target here.

findings.title: localeCompare depends on the locale
findings.body: Ties are broken by name; `localeCompare` can order accented names differently per machine. Compare code units for a stable order.

findings.title: The duplicate key ignores the sequence number
findings.body: Line 6 leaves out the sequence number, so two genuine postings with the same accounts and amount collapse into one.

findings.title: No journal can ever be unbalanced
findings.body: Line 11 adds and subtracts the same amount, so every journal sums to zero. Track debits and credits separately per journal.

findings.title: Unbalanced journals still move balances
findings.body: Lines 12 and 13 post every line before knowing whether its journal balances. The statement closes only balanced journals.
